messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE - gpu-314 reporting repeated Xid 13 / ECC correctable spikes; driver resets observed, P100/RTX-class. Alert severity: P1. Auto-evac suggestion: cordon + drain.

maya: acked. I’m on it, joining now. tagging @jordan for oncall handoff if it widens.

jordan: joining, thanks. any customer-facing impact yet?

sam: metrics show 30% increase in driver reset count across node group gpu-pool-prod-2 over the last 4m. Pod restarts up x3. No infra-wide throttles reported.

luis: checking customer request logs — 2 customers had elevated latency around 17:44 UTC, but no 5xx spike in API gateway. I’ll open a bridge if we need.

triage-bot: collected diagnostic bundle: /var/log/nvidia/gpu-314/driver-2024-05-08.tar.gz, dmesg snippet uploaded to https://telemetry.internal/logs/1745556666

maya: running quick health checks. kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-314 returns Ready but kubelet shows NotReady briefly.

jordan: recommend cordon/drain to prevent further OOMs and migrate workloads. Can one of you run drain and start a fallback routing policy?

sam: running drain now. command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-314 && kubectl drain gpu-314 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m```

sam: drain started. pods evicting, batch generation jobs are being rescheduled to gpu-pool-prod-1. Request router switching to fallback model variant 'redwood-small-v2' for affected tenants.

luis: notified impacted tenants: private-corp-A (low priority), analytics-startup-B (mid). Sending heads-up with ETA for mitigation.

maya: I’m grabbing driver logs and nvml traces. observed repeated `Xid 13: GPU exception` followed by `GPU reset required`. nv-host resets coincide with ECC correctable counters incrementing.

triage-bot: diagnostic snippet: ```May 08 17:42:12 gpu-314 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus. NVRM: RmEnableDevice FAILED!``` uploaded.

jordan: ok looks like a hardware-level ECC perturbation causing soft resets. Short term plan: keep node drained, monitor other nodes for correlated increases; escalate to HW ops for physical node inspection. Long term: consider isolating similar hardware batch.

maya: quick mitigation: set driver rollback to last known-good on next maintenance window? risky during P1. Alternative: enable ECC threshold-based proactive evacuation for the pool — will push policy via infra API.

eng-sre: pushed policy: `evacuate_on_corr_ecc=true` to gpu-pool-prod-2 with threshold 100 correctables/hour. Confirmed rollout to fleet manager.

sam: telemetry shows drains completed, customer latency normalizing for affected tenants. No 500s after reroute.

luis: customers acknowledged. analytics-startup-B asked for a postmortem and ETA for node return. I suggested 2-4 hours for HW ops triage + possible memory module reseat.

maya: started a temporary circuit breaker at router to prefer dedicated-capacity fallbacks for models with >2s tail latency. config: `fallback_policy: prefer_dedicated_but_fallback_to_small`.

triage-bot: pulled core dumps from containerized runtimes; attaching sample to the incident bundle. stack traces indicate kernel-level GPU reset, not container oom.

jordan: please triple-check quota / isolation so noisy tenants didn't cause memory pressure. Are we seeing any abnormal tensor allocation patterns?

sam: allocation heatmaps show a single job on gpu-314 with sustained large sequence lengths + batch size that increased KV cache churn. That workload coincides with first Xid spike. marking job id 9845 as noisy.

maya: I’ll contact the tenant (owner listed in scheduler metadata) to request reducing batch sizes and enabling streaming. Also will add a temp placement constraint so their jobs avoid gpu-pool-prod-2.

luis: sent customer note with recommended ML config tweaks. They responded that they can throttle for next 3 hours.

eng-sre: HW ops booked on-call to inspect gpu-314. ETA 1h 30m. If they find memory DIMM errors we’ll schedule host reboot + firmware update.

jordan: good. next steps checklist: 1) keep node cordoned and drained — done. 2) keep eviction policy active — done. 3) monitor fleet for correlated ECC bursts — Sam running watch. 4) HW ops inspect host — pending. 5) postmortem draft after closure — assign to maya.

maya: assigning postmortem to myself. I’ll include timeline, noisy job id, driver logs, and mitigation steps.

sam: monitoring alert cleared on pool after reroute. setting follow-up alert threshold lower for next 24h.

triage-bot: incident status: mitigation in progress, customers rerouted, HW ops en route. Recording for audit.

luis: customer bridge open? they asked for live bridge for 30m — I’ll host a short bridge at :30 if HW ops needs to update.

maya: thanks everyone. keeping channel open. will update when HW ops reports or if node trend worsens. :white_check_mark:
